title: Late-night stream drop + autoscale surge investigation
content:
Summary:

On 2029-11-05 02:14 UTC we observed a sharp, system-wide spike in streaming connection churn that resulted in a 12-minute window of elevated 5xx and significantly degraded p95/p99 token latencies for the hosted streaming API. Impact: ~18% of active streaming sessions experienced mid-stream disconnects with a recline/reconnect cycle; total request errors (5xx) increased by ~6x and p99 token latency rose from 220ms to 1.8s. Several customers reported partial transcript loss and reconnect loops.

Why this document exists:
This is an investigative draft that synthesizes telemetry, host logs, and on-call notes. It aims to (1) explain the chain of events, (2) capture live mitigations and their efficacy, and (3) enumerate actionable follow-ups and runbook changes to prevent recurrence.

High-level timeline (all timestamps UTC):
- 02:12:30 — First anomalous increase in TCP SYNs to edge (small spike observed in edge dashboard).
- 02:13:05 — Streaming session error rate begins rising on a subset of regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1). p95 starts creeping.
- 02:14:00 — On-call alert: streaming session error rate > 5x baseline for 60s (SRE-7482 triggered).
- 02:15:30 — Autoscaler begins scaling up ephemeral serving pools for streaming in affected regions.
- 02:16:10 — Multiple worker processes show elevated KV-cache eviction counts and KV-lock wait time spikes.
- 02:17:20 — Operator initiated mitigation: enable aggressive accept-throttling on front-end edge (temporary ingress rate-limit).
- 02:19:00 — Accept-throttling stabilizes new session acceptance; reconnect storms continue but new successful sessions drop by ~40%.
- 02:24:10 — Rolling rollback of the last serving-runtime config change (adaptive-batching beta toggle) started in eu-west-1 as test.
- 02:25:50 — Rollback shows immediate improvement in p95 but p99 remains elevated due to backlog and reconnect loops.
- 02:26:35 — KV-cache lock backlog reduces; p99 latency starts trending down.
- 02:26:40 — Incident declared mitigated to acceptable thresholds; monitoring kept a quiet watch until 02:36 before fully resolving.

Observed metrics (peak window 02:14–02:26):
- Streaming session churn rate: +520% vs baseline.
- 5xx rate (stream endpoints): +600% peak.
- p95 token latency: 220ms -> 660ms; p99: 220ms -> 1800ms.
- KV-cache eviction rate: +14x.
- Autoscaler scaled ephemeral pools from 120->340 instances in affected region over ~3m.
- Reconnect attempts per client median: 3x -> 11x in 2 minutes.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
A client-side reconnect wave (origin unknown; appears to be a multi-customer spike) caused a burst of short-lived streaming sessions. The edge layer tried to accept these reconnects which led to heavy churn. A recent change in the serving-runtime adaptive-batching path (merged in PR #4543) changed session prefetch behavior and introduced an interaction where ephemeral session setup performed synchronous KV-cache priming under a global KV lock. Under extreme churn the KV lock became contended, causing service threads to stall. The autoscaler reacted to the increased queueing/latency signals by provisioning more ephemeral workers, which increased the number of simultaneous KV priming operations, amplifying lock contention and eviction thrash — a positive feedback loop. The net effect: short-lived reconnections multiplied contention and tail latency, producing widespread reconnect storms and increased 5xx.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Correlated spike in KV-lock wait time (trace logs) with p99 latency peak.
- Heap of short-lived session creation traces — median session life ~9s during spike vs baseline 120s.
- PR #4543 (adaptive-batching prefetch) changed code path that now does KV priming under the same lock (tracebacks show new call chain).
- Regions with older runtime (no PR applied) had significantly less impact.
- Reverting adaptive-batching toggle in eu-west-1 produced rapid improvement in p95 and KV-lock metrics.

Contributing factors:
- Edge had no short-term reconnect-rate circuit breaker per client token; single clients initiating reconnect loops could drive disproportionate acceptance rates.
- Autoscaler tuning reacts to queueing/backpressure signals but lacks a dampening window for session-churn-driven queueing (i.e., it treats reconnection bursts like sustained load).
- KV priming being performed synchronously under a global lock increases coupling between session setup concurrency and runtime tail latency.
- Lack of a synthetic test that simulates reconnection storms during recent adaptive-batching integration.

Immediate mitigations applied (and who did them):
- 02:17:20 — Edge accept-throttling enabled for new streaming sessions in affected regions (on-call, Liam Brooks). Impact: reduced new accepted sessions by ~40%, buying time to reduce KV contention.
- 02:24:10 — Targeted rollback of adaptive-batching prefetch toggle in eu-west-1 (engineering, Rafael Silva). Impact: fast reduction in KV-lock wait time and p95 latency.
- 02:28:05 — Autoscaler soft-thresholds adjusted to ignore 30s of queueing spikes (SRE config change by Ava Chen). Impact: reduced overscale amplification.

Why the rollback worked:
Rolling back removed the synchronous KV priming call path that exercised the global lock heavily during session setup. This reduced the time each new session held the lock and allowed worker threads to progress, clearing backpressure without having to wait for autoscaler to completely settle.

Why the accept-throttle helped:
By limiting the rate of new session acceptance we limited the number of concurrent session setups hitting the hot KV path, buying time for an operator to perform the rollback and for in-flight backlogs to drain.

Longer-term fixes and action items (owner, ETA):
- Add per-client reconnect-rate circuit breaker at edge with exponential backoff enforcement (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2029-11-30).
- Rework KV priming to be async or to use sharded locks (owner: Rafael Silva, ETA: 2029-12-15).
- Add dampening in autoscaler to ignore short-lived queueing spikes under a 60s window and require sustained signal for scale-up (owner: Ava Chen, ETA: 2029-11-20).
- Add a synthetic workload in CI that injects reconnect storms and validates streaming stack behavior post-PR (owner: Miles Ortega, ETA: 2029-11-18).
- Update runbook: create a "reconnect-storm" play with step-by-step acceptance throttles, autoscaler dampening, and targeted rollback steps (owner: SRE runbook lead, Liam Brooks, ETA: 2029-11-12).
- Add trace and metric correlation dashboard (KV-lock wait time, session-setup latency, newly-accepted-session rate, autoscaler scale events) to primary incident page (owner: Observability team, ETA: 2029-11-13).
- Code PR to add a guarded adaptive-batching mode that disables synchronous priming when session churn threshold is crossed (owner: serving-runtime team, Rafael Silva, ETA: 2029-12-08).

Runbook edits (draft) — quick steps for on-call:
1) If streaming 5xx and p99 token latency spike together with short session lifetimes: suspect reconnect storm.
2) Immediately enable edge accept-throttling for new streaming sessions in affected region.
3) Check recent serving-runtime deploys/toggles. If adaptive-batching prefetch was toggled in last 24h, prepare targeted rollback.
4) If autoscaler is aggressively scaling, temporarily bump dampening window in SRE autoscaler config to 60–120s.
5) If KV-lock wait time > 500ms and eviction rate is high, escalate to serving-runtime on-call and consider rollback.
6) Communicate to CS (via incident template) with suggested user-facing wording and expected ETA of mitigation.

Communications / customer notes:
- Initial customer-facing note drafted by CS: "We briefly experienced streaming disruptions in some regions due to an internal service interaction. Our engineers applied mitigations and rolled back a config change; services are stable. We are investigating root cause and will follow up with details and remediation plans." (owner: Priya Nair).

Post-incident retro notes (observations):
- The positive-feedback loop (reconnect -> priming -> lock -> autoscale -> more priming) is a systemic risk that can be triggered by other short-lived event storms (e.g., ephemeral load tests, bot floods).
- Autoscaler acting on short window queueing without context about session duration/churn is generally unsafe for the streaming control-plane.
- Quick rollback of new code paths remains an effective first-order mitigation when correlation exists. We should make toggles easier to revert per-region.

Outstanding unknowns and follow-ups:
- Origin of reconnect wave: vendor CDNs and a few high-volume customers show increased reconnects in their client logs during the window. CS outreach in progress to correlate client SDK updates. (ticket: SRE-7482).
- Validate whether token exhaustion or client SDK bug contributed to mass reconnects. (owner: Solutions Eng, due 2029-11-12).

Appendix: useful queries and dashboards used during triage:
- Streaming: new-session-rate by edge.ip, client-token
- Traces: session-setup critical path, KV-lock wait spans
- Autoscaler: scale-up events timeline, scale speed, instance provision latency
- KV store: eviction rates, per-shard prime times
- Example log search that found short-lived sessions: 
  "service:streaming AND event:"session_start" AND duration_ms < 15000"

Owners for follow-ups (single-line summary):
- Edge circuit breaker implementation: Priya Nair
- Autoscaler dampening tuning and SRE config: Ava Chen
- KV priming code rework: Rafael Silva
- Runbook and incident template updates: Liam Brooks
- Customer outreach coordination: Priya Nair and Solutions Eng

Status of action items as of last_modified:
- Edge throttling: implemented during incident (temporary) — complete
- Rollback in eu-west-1: complete (partial region rollback) — complete
- Autoscaler dampening: temporary config applied during incident; permanent change in progress — in_progress
- Runbook draft: created in this doc — in_progress
- Synthetic reconnect test: test harness planned and being implemented — in_progress

If you have additional logs/traces to attach, paste links under linked_artifacts and ping the channel #sre-incident-2029-11-05-thread.

End of draft.
